exposure: biothermal stress (Universal Thermal Climate Index: heat stress, cold stress)
preconceptional thyrotropin levels (subnormal <0.37 mIU/L, supranormal >=4.88 mIU/L, normal)
cohort: The study included 6,218,131 singleton live births in China.
finding: Both heat stress and cold stress during each trimester were associated with increased risks of preterm birth, with a synergistic effect identified between biothermal stress and preconceptional thyrotropin abnormalities.
